You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Cross-cutting platform concepts.

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: The Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as single source of truth; document flow / document relationship browser; the Business Partner model (BP as single object for customer/vendor); output management; number ranges; the authorization concept (roles/profiles); multi-client architecture and SaaS multi-tenancy in S/4HANA Cloud.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Universal Journal pattern and document flow are MANDATORY inheritances (one append-only financial line-item table, FI/CO views as projections; every business document records predecessor/successor links with a UI chain viewer). Atlas keeps separate vendor and customer masters rather than a unified Business Partner (note this as a deliberate deviation). Row-level tenant_id multi-tenancy with non-bypassable session filter; JWT auth with roles -> permissions -> resources as data; append-only audit table via middleware; per-tenant document number sequences. Output management beyond basic document rendering is not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about S/4HANA Business Partner mandatory customer vendor integration (CVI):

## Overview

In S/4HANA, the Business Partner (BP) is the "single point of entry" for managing the master data of your customers and vendors. You can no longer create a customer or a vendor without first creating a Business Partner.

## Mandatory Nature

CVI is the mandatory process that synchronizes your existing customer and supplier master data with the Business Partner model in SAP S/4HANA. The migration of all creditors and debtors is not a matter of choice; it is mandatory.

## Key Process

The BP is created first, and the CVI process automatically creates the corresponding customer and/or vendor views in the background. The CVI component ensures the synchronization between the Business Partner object and the Customer/Vendor objects.

## System Conversion Requirements

For existing systems migrating to S/4HANA, before you can technically convert your system, you must first convert all your existing customers and vendors into Business Partners within your ECC system, which is a mandatory pre-conversion step.

## Data Quality Importance

CVI is a strict process that requires high-quality master data to work correctly. Inconsistent or incorrectly formatted data will cause errors and prevent the Business Partner from being created.

I've completed the web search for your query about S/4HANA Universal Journal ACDOCA single source of truth architecture. Here are the key findings:

## Overview

The Universal Journal is the architectural cornerstone of SAP S/4HANA, serving as the central financial steering model that provides a financial single source of truth for an organization.

## Core Architecture

The Universal Journal captures line-item details in table ACDOCA, which serves as a unified table that consolidates financial and controlling data. The Universal Journal combines information from the general ledger, any special ledgers, controlling, asset accounting, and the material ledger.

## Single Source of Truth Benefits

The Universal journal entry eliminates the need for the separation made previously between Financial Accounting (FI) and Controlling (CO), and since financial accounting and managerial accounting are reconciled constantly, there is no longer any need for reconciliation between FI and CO or between FI-GL and FI-AA.

Combining the data structures of the different components into a single line item table (ACDOCA) results in a single source of truth that replaces the previously separate physical tables.

## Key Features

The ACDOCA table contains all fields needed for G/L, CO, AA, ML, PA and thus it is called a single source of truth and follows on the fly calculations process. Additionally, table ACDOCP is designed to extend the Universal Journal to store plan data and is structurally designed in the same way as table ACDOCA, but with the purpose of incorporating all plan data so that you can run actual-plan comparisons.

## Architecture and Configuration

In SAP S/4HANA, the target architecture is based on Adobe Document Server and Adobe Forms only. For the form determination rules (along with other output parameters) BRF+ functionality is used (in this sense in combination with the message determination).

## Output Management Framework

With SAP S/4HANA a new Output Management approach is in place. By design, the new output management includes cloud qualities such as extensibility enablement, multi tenancy enablement and modification free configuration. It is designed to be the successor for all frameworks (such as SD, FI Correspondence, CRM post processing).

## Key Configuration Components

When the business rules are applied by Output Management, attributes obtained from the document are used to determine the type of output, the receiver of output, the channel used to issue the output, the printer settings (only applicable for output channel PRINT) and the form template used to generate a PDF document.

## Prerequisites

Adobe Document Server is available – ADS needs to be implemented to allow SAP to fetch PDF properties for rendering output form. Transaction code KPRO has to be maintained with the help of Basis – KPRO allows to store PDF attachments on physical location.

## Form Templates

The master form template contains static data (such as a logo and footer) that is applied to each form page and is determined based on configuration setting maintained.

I've performed the web search for your query about SAP S/4HANA Cloud multi-tenancy, client concept, authorization roles, PFCG, and business roles. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Authorization Concept Overview

SAP S/4HANA Cloud handles role and restriction management by using a predefined set of business catalogs and roles delivered by SAP, which can be adopted or customized as needed.

## Business Roles vs. PFCG

Unlike traditional systems, where roles and permissions are heavily dependent on complex PFCG authorizations, S/4HANA allows for a more intuitive model using a Web UI for defining business roles through a combination of catalogs and restriction values.

SAP S/4HANA Cloud simplifies the role assignment by introducing business catalogs as the smallest assignable entity. Those business catalogs represent the building blocks for maintaining business roles.

## Business Catalogs and Restrictions

Business catalogs represent semantically meaningful tasks within a business process and are linked to authorizations through the Fiori-PFCG integration. Business catalogs in the S/4HANA Cloud authorization model are crucial because they divide S/4HANA business functionality into "building blocks" representing tasks or sub-processes, facilitating the assignment of authorizations.

Administrators control write and read access by maintaining restrictions at the catalog level for the SAP Fiori apps, dashboards, and other data access assigned within the business catalog.

## Multi-Tenancy and Cloud Implementation

S/4HANA Cloud, public edition is a closely knit landscape of multiple tenants and access is granted in each tenant during respective phases of implementation journey.

Based on the search results, I found information about several key topics related to SAP S/4HANA document management:

## Document Flow

Document flow gives you an overview of how far a commercial transaction has progressed as well as the follow-on documents related to the transaction. Depending on where you choose to view the document flow from, the system displays all preceding and follow-on documents on the document flow screen.

## Number Ranges

The document number range defines the intervals of numbers utilized in document numbering and it is crucial to ensure that these number ranges don't overlap. SAP S/4HANA allows for two types of number assignments: Internal Numbering where SAP S/4HANA keeps a record of the last document number generated by the customized number range in the Current Number field, and the system then assigns the number succeeding the current number as the subsequent document number. External Number Assignment allows the user to manually input the original document number, or it can be transferred from another system, and as the numbers aren't allotted in a sequence, SAP S/4HANA does not preserve a current number.

## Audit Considerations

This is particularly valuable during audits because it provides a clear record of who reviewed and approved each transaction. Additionally, using external number ranges has its own set of disadvantages like missing numbers, non-sequential number patterns that give birth to audit issues, legal complications etc.

input.overview: Cross-cutting platform concepts in S/4HANA (2025/2026) are the architectural primitives every functional module relies on: the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as the single financial line-item table replacing separate FI/CO/AA/ML tables; document flow with predecessor/successor links viewable in the Document Relationship Browser; the mandatory unified Business Partner model (CVI-synchronized customer/vendor views); the BRF+/Adobe Forms output management framework; configurable number ranges per document type; the roles/profiles authorization concept (PFCG on-premise, business roles and catalogs with restrictions in Cloud); and the client (MANDT) field on nearly every table on-premise, replaced by tenant isolation in S/4HANA Cloud SaaS. Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning, and consulting sources) supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge for change documents, workflow, and extensibility. Atlas v1 deliberately inherits the two load-bearing patterns (Universal Journal, document flow) and covers tenancy, RBAC, audit, and numbering, while consciously deviating on the Business Partner model and deferring output management, workflow, and extensibility.

capabilities.capability: Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as single source of truth
capabilities.description: One line-item table unifying G/L, controlling, asset accounting, material ledger, and profitability analysis, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation; plan data mirrored in ACDOCP.
Every business document records its preceding and follow-on documents (quote -> order -> delivery -> invoice -> accounting doc), navigable as a chain in the UI.

Single mandatory master-data object for customers and vendors; CVI synchronizes BP roles to customer/vendor views, enabling one party to be both, with shared addresses, relationships, and time-dependent data.
capabilities.reason: Deliberate deviation: Atlas v1 keeps separate vendor and customer master tables; customer/vendor master data itself is planned, but there is no unified party object, no shared roles/relationships, and no single identity for an entity that is both customer and supplier.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a thin party/business-partner table that links existing customer and vendor records as roles, without restructuring the two masters.

capabilities.capability: Output management (determination rules, channels, form templates)
capabilities.description: BRF+ rule-driven determination of output type, recipient, channel (print/email/EDI/XML), and form template (Adobe Forms with master templates), with output status, queue, and reprocessing across all document types.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only basic document rendering; the rule-based determination framework, multi-channel dispatch (email/EDI), template management, and output status/retry queue are explicitly not in the v1 list.
capabilities.later_path: Add a rule-driven output determination service (document attributes -> channel + template + recipient) with pluggable channel adapters and a retryable output queue.

capabilities.description: Configurable number intervals per document type with internal (system-assigned sequential) or external assignment; non-overlapping ranges and gapless sequences where legally required.
capabilities.later_path: Add external number assignment and per-fiscal-year ranges later if conversion/legal scenarios demand them.

capabilities.description: PFCG roles bundling authorization objects on-premise; business roles composed of business catalogs with read/write restrictions (org-level values like company code, plant) in S/4HANA Cloud.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans the RBAC core (JWT auth, roles -> permissions -> resources stored as data), but S/4HANA's field/org-value restrictions (scoping a permission to specific company codes, plants, etc.) and segregation-of-duties analysis are not in the v1 list.
capabilities.later_path: Extend permission records with attribute/scope filters (org-unit values) evaluated alongside the tenant filter, then layer SoD rule checks on role assignments.

capabilities.description: On-premise: client (MANDT) key on nearly all tables isolates independent business environments in one system; S/4HANA Cloud: dedicated tenants on shared infrastructure with strict isolation.
Change documents (CDHDR/CDPOS) record who changed which field from what to what on master and transactional objects, plus security audit log, supporting compliance and audits.
capabilities.later_path: Add read-access logging for sensitive fields as a later compliance increment.

capabilities.capability: Extensibility framework (custom fields, key-user and side-by-side extensions)
capabilities.description: In-app/key-user extensibility for custom fields and logic on released business contexts, plus side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP via released APIs and events, all upgrade-stable.
capabilities.reason: No custom-field or extension mechanism appears anywhere in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 ships fixed schemas only.
capabilities.later_path: Add JSONB custom-field columns with metadata-driven validation on core entities, plus webhook/event hooks per document type.

capabilities.description: Cross-application workflow (classic SAP Business Workflow and Fiori flexible workflows) for approvals and multi-step processes, e.g. PO release, journal entry verification, with My Inbox integration.
capabilities.reason: No approval/workflow capability is in the Atlas v1 plan; documents post directly without configurable release strategies, which practitioners consider a core control in procurement and finance.
capabilities.later_path: Add a generic approval service (document type + condition -> ordered approver steps) driving a status field that blocks posting until approved.

capabilities.description: Stable, versioned OData/SOAP APIs (SAP Business Accelerator Hub) and business events for integrating S/4HANA with external systems; the backbone of clean-core integration.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 cross-cutting scope defines internal patterns (journal, flow, tenancy, auth) but lists no public API contract or event emission for external integration.
capabilities.later_path: Publish the existing internal REST endpoints as a versioned public API and emit domain events (document created/changed) to a message bus or webhooks.

content.text: Research complete. Structured output delivered with 11 capabilities assessed against the Atlas v1 scope, based on live web research of SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and SAP Learning sources.
